controls.title: Harden and isolate directory infrastructure
controls.statement: Use domain controllers and related identity servers only for their security roles, remove unnecessary services and protocols, and place them in protected network and management paths.
controls.risk: If a domain controller or related identity server is compromised, an attacker could take control of authentication across the organisation and gain broad access to systems and information.
controls.scope: Microsoft AD DS domain controllers, AD CS, AD FS and Microsoft Entra Connect servers, including their installed software, enabled services, network paths and administration interfaces.
controls.examine: Compare the approved identity architecture and hardened build standards with installed applications, enabled roles and services, network rules, administrative paths and current configuration records.
controls.interview: Ask directory and infrastructure owners how additional software is prevented, how management traffic reaches identity servers and how insecure or obsolete services are identified and removed.
controls.test: Sample each identity-server role and verify that only approved security functions are installed, unnecessary services are disabled and administration is possible only through the authorised management path.
test_steps: Select at least one server from each deployed identity role and compare its installed roles, applications, services, ports and network interfaces with the approved hardened build.
Verify unnecessary services such as Print Spooler and obsolete protocols are disabled, then use safe discovery from an adjacent network to confirm only approved ports respond.
Attempt authorised administration from both an approved management host and an ordinary workstation; confirm only the protected route reaches management interfaces.
Review configuration and change records for any deviation, confirming it has a current owner, approved reason, compensating control and expiry date.
controls.expected: Identity servers perform only approved security functions, expose only required services and accept administration only from protected management paths.

mappings.basis: Restricts AD DS domain controllers, AD CS, AD FS and Entra Connect servers to their designed roles and security-related applications or services.
Requires the Print Spooler service to be disabled on AD DS domain controllers.
Restricts domain controllers to AD DS and prohibits non-security-related services and applications.
Requires SMB version 1 to be disabled on domain controllers.
Requires systems to provide only mission-essential capabilities and restrict unnecessary functions, ports, protocols, software and services.

controls.title: Restrict Active Directory administrative access
controls.statement: Limit directory administration to named people with a current need, use dedicated administrative accounts, and allow privileged access only from protected workstations or jump servers.
controls.risk: An attacker who compromises a directory administrator could create trusted accounts, change security policy and take control of connected systems.
controls.scope: Directory administrators, privileged security groups, administrative accounts, secure administrative workstations, jump servers and management connections to identity infrastructure.
controls.examine: Reconcile approved administrators with Domain Admins, Enterprise Admins and equivalent groups, dedicated account inventories, workstation assignments, jump-server rules and privileged access logs.
controls.interview: Ask directory owners who can approve administrative access, how ordinary and privileged duties are separated and how urgent or temporary access is removed.
controls.test: Sample directory administrators and trace their approval, dedicated account, protected workstation and permitted management route. Confirm that an ordinary account or unapproved workstation cannot administer a domain controller.
test_steps: Export current membership of Domain Admins, Enterprise Admins and equivalent delegated groups and reconcile it with named approvals, owners and expiry dates.
For sampled administrators, verify separate ordinary and domain-administration accounts, an assigned secure workstation or jump server and no privileged sign-ins from ordinary devices.
Attempt a benign directory read and approved administrative change from an authorised management host, then repeat the privileged attempt from an unapproved host and ordinary account.
Confirm the approved route is attributable and logged, the unapproved routes fail, and temporary or obsolete group membership has been removed from effective access.
controls.expected: Every directory administrator has a current approved need, uses a dedicated account from an authorised management device and cannot reach directory administration through ordinary access paths.

mappings.basis: Requires domain controllers to be administered with dedicated domain administrator accounts that are not used to administer other systems.
Limits access to AD DS, AD CS, AD FS and Entra Connect servers to privileged users who require it.
Requires membership of Domain Admins, Enterprise Admins and other highly privileged groups to be minimised.
Limits domain-controller access to privileged users who require access.
Restricts privileged paths to domain controllers to jump servers and secure administrative workstations using only required ports and services.
Restricts privileged accounts to authorised personnel or roles.
Requires least privilege to be enforced for administrative users and service accounts.

controls.title: Secure service accounts and delegation
controls.statement: Identify and assign owners to directory service accounts, use managed credentials where supported, grant only the permissions they need, prevent unnecessary delegation or directory replication rights, and review DCSync permissions at least every six months.
controls.risk: A weak or over-privileged service account could let an attacker move through the domain, obtain more powerful credentials and retain access without using a personal account.
controls.scope: Service and computer accounts, service principal names, group Managed Service Accounts, delegation settings, DCSync permissions, credentials, owners and review records.
controls.examine: Compare service-account inventories and owners with SPN registrations, gMSA use, group memberships, effective permissions, DCSync rights, delegation settings and the dates and outcomes of permission reviews.
controls.interview: Ask application and directory owners how service accounts are created, how managed credentials are selected, how excessive permissions or delegation are removed and how six-monthly DCSync reviews are completed.
controls.test: Sample service and computer accounts, verify ownership and purpose, inspect their effective privileges and delegation, and confirm that credentials rotate through the managed process without being known or reused by people.
test_steps: Build a sample from accounts with service principal names, gMSAs, computer accounts, delegation settings and DCSync-capable permissions, including dormant and high-privilege cases.
For each account, verify a current owner and purpose, managed credential use where supported, recent rotation, minimum group membership and no interactive use unless explicitly required.

Inspect effective replication rights and constrained or unconstrained delegation; confirm DCSync-capable accounts were reviewed within six months and use an authorised query to test that sampled accounts cannot exceed their documented function.
For one managed account, observe a scheduled credential rotation or controlled rollover and confirm the dependent service continues without exposing the secret to an operator.
controls.expected: Each service account has a current owner and purpose, uses a managed credential where supported, holds only required access and has no unnecessary DCSync or delegation capability. DCSync permissions are reviewed at least every six months.

mappings.basis: Requires service accounts to be created as group Managed Service Accounts.
Prohibits DCSync permissions for service accounts configured with a service principal name.
Prohibits non-domain-controller computer accounts from being trusted for delegation to services.
Calls for accounts with service principal names to use gMSAs, or strong managed passwords where gMSAs are not feasible.
Requires user objects with DCSync permissions to be reviewed every six months to confirm that the permissions remain necessary.

mappings.uid: asd-ad:appendix a §mitigating an unconstrained delegation compromise#1
mappings.basis: Requires computer objects not to be configured for unconstrained delegation.
Requires an owned inventory of service accounts and recurring reviews that accounts remain authorised.
Requires stronger credentials, multi-factor authentication or single-use credentials for higher-risk access, including service accounts.

controls.title: Harden directory authentication, root credentials and trusts
controls.statement: Require protected directory authentication, change the KRBTGT password twice at least every six months and after suspected domain compromise, remove obsolete protocols, and allow trusts only when their security boundaries are explicit and enforced.
controls.risk: Weak authentication, stale domain root credentials or an unsafe trust could allow an attacker to forge access, impersonate users and cross into systems that should remain separate.
controls.scope: KRBTGT credentials, Kerberos and LDAP configuration, NTLM and SMB protocols, domain and forest trusts, SID filtering, connected identity systems and IT-to-OT identity boundaries.
controls.examine: Review KRBTGT change records, domain authentication policy, protocol configuration, LDAP signing, Kerberos pre-authentication exceptions, trust inventory, trust direction, SID filtering and connected-environment architecture.
controls.interview: Ask directory and system owners how the two-step KRBTGT change is coordinated, why each legacy protocol, authentication exception and trust exists, and how continued need is reviewed.
controls.test: Verify the most recent two-step KRBTGT rotation and replication evidence, use authorised checks for LDAP signing and Kerberos pre-authentication, identify attempted use of prohibited protocols, and confirm selected trusts enforce their approved direction and SID filtering.
test_steps: Review the last two-step KRBTGT change and replication evidence, confirm it occurred within six months or promptly after suspected compromise, then review LDAP signing, Kerberos pre-authentication, NTLM, SMBv1 and trust policy.

Use authorised protocol tests to attempt unsigned LDAP, prohibited NTLM or SMBv1 and a Kerberos sign-in for sampled accounts; confirm insecure paths are rejected or constrained by an approved exception.
Enumerate domain and forest trusts and test selected cross-boundary authentication in both directions, confirming the documented direction, scope and SID filtering.
Trace failed legacy-protocol and trust-boundary attempts to monitoring, and verify every exception has an owner, business need, expiry date and compensating control.
controls.expected: KRBTGT credentials are changed twice at least every six months and after suspected compromise, directory authentication uses approved protected protocols, and each trust is necessary and technically constrained.

mappings.basis: Requires LDAP signing on AD DS domain controllers.
Requires Kerberos pre-authentication for user accounts.
Requires SID Filtering for domain and forest trusts.
Requires two KRBTGT credential changes with domain-controller replication between them after suspected compromise or when six months have elapsed.
Requires LDAP signing on domain controllers.
Requires the NTLM protocol to be disabled.

mappings.uid: asd-ad:appendix a §mitigating a sid history compromise#3
mappings.basis: Requires SID Filtering for domain and forest trusts.
Requires the KRBTGT password to be changed every six months and after actual or suspected domain compromise.
Calls for separate IT and OT domain controllers without trusts and for built-in remote maintenance to be disabled or closely monitored.

controls.title: Monitor and protect recovery of identity infrastructure
controls.statement: Centrally collect and review security events from directory infrastructure, and maintain encrypted, access-controlled backups needed to rebuild trusted identity services.
controls.risk: A directory compromise may remain undetected or leave the organisation unable to restore trusted access to critical services.
controls.scope: Security events and backups for AD DS domain controllers, AD CS, AD FS and Microsoft Entra Connect, including log pipelines, alerts, storage, encryption and administrative access.
controls.examine: Compare critical identity systems with log-source coverage, event selections, alert and investigation records, backup schedules, encryption settings, storage locations, access lists and recovery procedures.
controls.interview: Ask monitoring and recovery owners how directory attacks are detected, who can access identity backups and how they establish that retained copies can support a trusted rebuild.
controls.test: Generate an authorised security event and trace it into central monitoring, then sample recent backup jobs and verify successful completion, encryption, restricted access and availability to the documented recovery process.
test_steps: Generate authorised security events on AD DS, AD CS, AD FS and Entra Connect where deployed, including a failed privileged sign-in and a protected configuration change.
Trace each event to central monitoring and confirm source, actor, target, timestamp and outcome are preserved and a relevant detection rule creates the expected alert or investigation.
Select recent backups for each identity role and verify job success, encryption, isolated storage, retention and access limited to authorised backup or recovery personnel.
In an isolated recovery exercise or from recent evidence, verify the backup can supply the directory data and configuration needed by the documented trusted-rebuild sequence.
controls.expected: Relevant identity events reach central monitoring in time for investigation, and current protected backups are available only to authorised recovery personnel.

mappings.basis: Requires security-relevant events from AD DS domain controllers, AD CS, AD FS and Entra Connect to be centrally logged.
Requires backups of identity servers to use ASD-approved encryption, secure storage and access limited to backup administrators.
Requires domain-controller backups to be encrypted, securely stored and accessible only to Backup Administrators.
Requires domain-controller logs to be centrally logged and analysed promptly for malicious activity.
Requires organisations to identify and coordinate the event types needed to support audit and investigation.
Requires audit records to be reviewed and analysed for unusual activity and findings to be reported.
Requires backups of system information and documentation and protection of backup confidentiality, integrity and availability.
Requires audit logging to be enabled across enterprise assets through the audit-log management process.

controls.title: Control Active Directory key credentials
controls.statement: Restrict who can modify the msDS-KeyCredentialLink attribute, minimise privileged group membership and delegated permissions, monitor changes, and regularly identify key credentials that are not part of an approved passwordless authentication service.
controls.risk: An attacker who adds a hidden key credential could impersonate a user or computer and keep access even after the account password is changed.
controls.scope: User and computer objects, the msDS-KeyCredentialLink attribute, Domain Admins, Key Admins and Enterprise Key Admins, delegated permissions, passwordless authentication services and directory change events.
controls.examine: Compare authorised passwordless authentication services and privileged groups with effective rights to modify msDS-KeyCredentialLink, current attribute values, event 5136 records, alerts, investigation results and recurring review evidence.
controls.interview: Ask directory and identity owners which services may add key credentials, how delegated rights are approved, how unexpected values or changes are detected and how often all objects are reviewed.
controls.test: Reconcile every principal that can modify msDS-KeyCredentialLink, inspect objects for unexplained key credentials, and use an authorised test object to confirm an approved change is logged and an unapproved principal cannot make the same change.
test_steps: Export effective rights to modify msDS-KeyCredentialLink and membership of Domain Admins, Key Admins and Enterprise Key Admins, then reconcile each principal to a current owner, approval and business need.
Query user and computer objects for key credentials and investigate a risk-based sample of multiple, recent or unexpected values against records from approved passwordless authentication services.
On an authorised test object, add and remove a key credential through the approved workflow, confirm event 5136 records the actor, object and attribute, and trace the event into central monitoring.

Attempt the same benign modification with an unapproved test principal, confirm it is denied, and verify periodic reviews record unexplained credentials, investigation decisions and completed removal actions.
controls.expected: Only approved principals and services can add key credentials, every value can be explained, unauthorised changes are denied or detected, and recurring reviews remove unexplained credentials.

mappings.basis: Restricts membership of Domain Admins, Key Admins and Enterprise Key Admins, whose members can modify key credentials on directory objects.
Requires delegated permissions that can modify msDS-KeyCredentialLink to be reviewed and minimised.
Requires regular reviews of directory objects for unauthorised key credentials.
Requires membership of Domain Admins, Enterprise Admins and other highly privileged groups to be minimised.
Requires permissions to be limited to authorised access necessary for assigned functions.
Requires systems to generate audit records for selected security events with the defined record content.
Requires access rights to be defined and recurring reviews to confirm that privileges remain authorised.
Requires access permissions and authorisations to be managed, enforced and reviewed using least privilege and separation of duties.
